newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, February 21.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories in the Irish press on Friday.
- Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn on Thursday night beefed up the power of the Revenue Commissioners to begin a new three way attack on tax dodgers.
- Ireland's President Mary Robinson is again being tipped as a front-runner for a top United Nations post.
- All junior Irish ministers have been firmly warned not to break ranks when unveiling new plans or policies.
- A world breakthrough in detecting BSE in beef carcasses before it can enter the food chain was claimed on Thursday by an Irish research company.

- SDLP leader John Hume on Thursday made an unusually scathing attack on Sinn Fein and the IRA, questioning their good faith and warning the electorate that a vote for Sinn Fein was in effect a vote for violence.

- The commissions paid on share dealing to stockbrokers by Irish investment managers leaped by 45 percent to 8.7 million Irish pounds last year on the back of a strong bull market which in total was worth over 15 million Irish pounds to brokers.
- For the first time in 25 years, the British government has signalled that a new investigation could be held into the events of Bloody Sunday.

- Irish nationalist and labour politicians have expressed anger, confusion and disbelief at comments by Sir Edward Heath, the former British Prime Minister, in which he linked the massacre in Tiananmen Square in China with the events of Bloody Sunday.
- Ireland's Aer Rianta has completed the acquisition of a 40 percent stake in Birmingham Airport, along with its joint-venture partner, NatWest Ventures.
- In a surprise move, IDA Ireland has withdrawn a letter to the parliamentary committee considering a law imposing a 48-hour working week.
- The leader of the opposition Irish Fianna Fail party, Bertie Ahern, has set out his party's support for the single currency in very strong terms.
- Two female civil servants on Thursday won the first round of an historic equality test case against the Irish Department of Finance, which could have far-reaching implications.
- Seventeen months of trauma for an Irish-based mother, whose child was abducted by his father, finally came to an end on Thursday in the courtroom of a tiny island in the Pacific Ocean.

- SDLP leader John Hume said on Thursday night his efforts with Gerry Adams to bring about restoration of the IRA cease-fire would continue despite his sharp rejection of an electoral pact with Sinn Fein.
- The outlook for export growth in 1997 is generally favourable, according to Alan McQuaid, chief economist with Bloxham Stockbrokers.
